## Summary

I analyzed session `sub-Jenkins_ses-20090912` from DANDI Dandiset [000070](https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/000070) (Churchland lab center-out reaching task with 192 M1/PMd units, streamed via `remfile`), demonstrating both reach-direction and velocity tuning:

- **Discrete direction tuning**: fit a Georgopoulos cosine model to 348 straight single-target reaches; found units with up to R²=0.91, preferred directions spread across the full circle in both M1 and PMd.
- **Continuous velocity/speed tuning**: computed instantaneous hand velocity across all 1573 successful reaches (including curved obstacle trials) and built Pynapple tuning curves — 116/192 units showed |correlation| > 0.7 between firing rate and speed (max r=0.98), and units also showed continuous movement-direction tuning.

All 7 figures were visually inspected and two layout bugs (polar-plot title overlap, a doubled axes frame from mixing `plt.subplot` with `subplots()`) were found and fixed.

Outputs in this directory: `reach_tuning_analysis.py` (jupytext script), `reach_tuning_analysis.ipynb` (executed notebook, no errors), `fig01`–`fig07.png`, and `README.md`.
